rows.jp: いくつかの坂を越えて、商店街に。
rows.en: After crossing several hills, I reach the shopping district.

ghs.en: Crossing over a fair number of hills, I reach the shopping street.

rows.jp: 人影はない。
rows.en: Not a soul in sight.

ghs.en: Not the shadow of a person.

rows.jp: 田崎商店が見える。
rows.en: Tazaki Store comes into view.

ghs.en: The Tasaki Store is in sight.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: ある種の期待とともに店内をのぞく。
rows.en: I peer inside with a certain anticipation.

ghs.en: I peek inside the store holding some kind of expectation.

rows.jp: だが、そこに人の息吹は感じられない。
rows.en: But I sense no breath of life within.

ghs.en: Yet, I could feel not even the breath of someone in there.
ghs.assessment: The source says he senses no human presence inside. 'Feel not even the breath of someone' is an unnatural negative construction and over-literalizes 息吹.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But I sense no human presence inside.'

highlights.text: Yet, I could feel not even the breath of someone in there.

rows.jp: 「……不在か」
rows.en: “...Nobody home.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...unmanned?"

rows.jp: 田崎食料はここしばらく、不在続き。
rows.en: Tazaki Foods has been unattended for some time now.

ghs.en: Tasaki Groceries had been repeatedly left unmanned recently.

rows.jp: この地域密着型ショップの店主　田崎吾一郎氏（４７歳独身）は無類の鉄道マニア。
rows.en: The owner of this little community shop, Goichiro Tazaki—forty-seven and single—is an inveterate railway fanatic.

ghs.en: The shopkeeper of this local-contact shop is a Tasaki Goichirou (age 47, single), unrivaled railway enthusiast.
ghs.assessment: 地域密着型 means community-oriented, not 'local-contact.' Calling him 'a Tasaki Goichirou' also wrongly treats the named proprietor as one arbitrary example.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The proprietor of this community shop is Tasaki Goichirou, forty-seven and single...'

highlights.text: The shopkeeper of this local-contact shop is a Tasaki Goichirou (age 47, single), unrivaled railway enthusiast.

rows.jp: よくふらりと店をあけ、遠方の土地にローカル線の写真を撮りに行く。
rows.en: He often wanders off, leaving the shop unattended while he travels to distant places to photograph local rail lines.

ghs.en: He must've casually opened the store, then trundled off to some faraway place to take pictures of their local train line.
ghs.assessment: The source says he often leaves the shop unattended and goes far away to photograph local railways. The English says he must have opened the store and describes one conjectural trip, reversing the habitual abandonment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'He often leaves the shop unattended and wanders off to photograph local railways in distant places.'

highlights.text: He must've casually opened the store, then trundled off to some faraway place to take pictures of their local train line.

rows.jp: たまに写真を見せびらかされるが、ちっとも楽しくない。
rows.en: Sometimes he shows the pictures off to me, but they do absolutely nothing for me.

ghs.en: Occasionally he did flaunt one of his photos at me, but that didn't seem really interesting.
ghs.assessment: The source states habitually that he sometimes shows off the photos and the narrator finds it no fun at all. The English shifts to sporadic past and weakens certainty to 'didn't seem really interesting.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Sometimes he shows them off to me, but I don't enjoy it at all.'

highlights.text: Occasionally he did flaunt one of his photos at me, but that didn't seem really interesting.

rows.jp: こっちは電車に抱く幻想など持ち合わせない今っ子なのだ。
rows.en: I’m a modern kid, with no romantic illusions about trains.

ghs.en: For this boy right now, fantasies to be entertained on trains are a product out of stock.
ghs.assessment: The narrator calls himself a modern kid who has no romantic fantasies about trains. 'Fantasies to be entertained on trains' changes the object of fantasy into its location and is syntactically opaque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm a modern kid with no romantic fantasies about trains.'

highlights.text: For this boy right now, fantasies to be entertained on trains are a product out of stock.

rows.jp: 店は店主不在時もあいている。
rows.en: The shop stays open even when its owner is away.

ghs.en: A shop open even with shopkeeper absent.
ghs.assessment: The source states that the shop remains open even when its owner is absent. 'A shop open even with shopkeeper absent' omits required articles and the finite verb.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The shop stays open even when the owner is away.'

highlights.text: A shop open even with shopkeeper absent.

rows.jp: 道楽的な無人商店だ。
rows.en: An unmanned store run as a hobby.

ghs.en: A clerk-less store that smells of profligacy.
ghs.assessment: 道楽的 describes the unmanned shop as an indulgent hobby operation. 'Smells of profligacy' adds a moralized accusation of wasteful vice.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's an unmanned shop run more as a hobby.'

highlights.text: A clerk-less store that smells of profligacy.

rows.jp: ２０代の頃ＪＲへの就職に失敗し時代遅れのヤンキーへと失墜した氏だが（三十路までこの愚行は続いた）、ご両親の死後しばらくを経て、険の取れた豊かな顔つきへと変わっていった。
rows.en: In his twenties, Mr. Tazaki failed to land a job with JR and sank into life as an anachronistic delinquent—a folly he sustained into his thirties—but some time after his parents died, the hard edges left his face and gave way to a mellow look of prosperity.

ghs.en: When he was in his 20s, his failure to find employment in the Japan Railways abased him into a delayed life of delinquency (a folly that continued until he was in his 30s), but sometime after the death of his parents, his face changed into one of abundance, its harshness lost.

rows.jp: 遺産以外の何が、元暴走族の粗暴な鉄オタを善人に変えうるというのか。
rows.en: What but an inheritance could turn a brutish ex-bosozoku train nerd into a decent human being?

ghs.en: Something outside the inheritance has changed someone who's more of a member of a biker gang than a railway fanatic into a nice guy, perhaps.
ghs.assessment: The source rhetorically says nothing but inheritance could have turned the rough former biker-gang railfan into a good man. The English claims something outside the inheritance did so and changes his combined traits into a comparison between them.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What but an inheritance could turn a rough former biker-gang railfan into a good man?'

highlights.text: Something outside the inheritance has changed someone who's more of a member of a biker gang than a railway fanatic into a nice guy, perhaps.

rows.jp: とにかく目先の現金にだけはありあまっている氏の店は、近隣の住人に対してはいくらでもツケてくれる希有な地元密着型店舗なのである。
rows.en: At any rate, Mr. Tazaki is swimming in ready cash, and his rare little neighborhood institution will let any local resident run up as large a tab as they please.

ghs.en: Anyway, the store owned by this man with more than enough cash underhand is one of those very rare, local-contact type stores that allows an unlimited tab for those who live around it.
ghs.assessment: 目先の現金 means ready cash on hand. 'Cash underhand' suggests illicit money, adding corruption absent from the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'this man with more ready cash than he knows what to do with.'

highlights.text: Anyway, the store owned by this man with more than enough cash underhand is one of those very rare, local-contact type stores that allows an unlimited tab for those who live around it.

rows.jp: だから人がいないのは珍しいことではない。
rows.en: So finding no one here is nothing unusual.

ghs.en: Therefore, there being nobody in here is no rare sight.

rows.jp: そういえば、ちょっと喉が渇いたな。
rows.en: Come to think of it, I am a little thirsty.

ghs.en: Speaking of which, my throat is a bit parched.
ghs.assessment: そういえば means 'come to think of it.' 'Speaking of which' incorrectly treats the previous subject as a conversational segue.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Come to think of it, I'm a little thirsty.'

highlights.text: Speaking of which, my throat is a bit parched.

rows.jp: 店の奥に行って、緑茶のボトルを一本取ってくる。
rows.en: I go to the back of the store and take a bottle of green tea.

ghs.en: I go into the depths of the store, and take out one bottle of green tea.
ghs.assessment: 店の奥 is the back of the store. 'The depths of the store' adds exaggerated spatial imagery.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I go to the back of the store and take a bottle of green tea.'

highlights.text: I go into the depths of the store, and take out one bottle of green tea.

rows.jp: メモ帳を取り出し、ペンを走らせる。
rows.en: I pull out a notepad and put pen to paper.

ghs.en: Taking out a notebook, I make the pen run.
ghs.assessment: ペンを走らせる simply means he writes quickly. 'Make the pen run' is an opaque literal calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I take out a notepad and start writing.'

highlights.text: Taking out a notebook, I make the pen run.

rows.jp: 『９／７、大緑茶、１３０円……黒須太一』
rows.en: “September 7—Big Green Tea—¥130—Taichi Kurosu.”

ghs.en:
9/7
Green King Tea
130￥
Kurosu Taichi
ghs.assessment: The product name 大緑茶 is 'Great/Big Green Tea.' 'Green King Tea' replaces the defining character with an unsupported royal title.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Great Green Tea.'

highlights.text:
9/7
Green King Tea
130￥
Kurosu Taichi

rows.jp: 壁にぺたりこ。
rows.en: Slap. Onto the wall it goes.

ghs.en: I stick the note to the wall.

rows.jp: 見ると、もう何枚ものメモが張ってある。
rows.en: I see that several other notes are already posted there.

ghs.en: Looking closer, there are several of these memos are up already.
ghs.assessment: 'There are several of these memos are up' contains two competing finite constructions and is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Looking closer, several memos are already posted there.'

highlights.text: Looking closer, there are several of these memos are up already.

rows.jp: 合宿中はいろいろ買いにきてたんだっけ。
rows.en: That’s right—we bought all sorts of things here during camp.

ghs.en: Seems we came here several times to buy things during the Training Camp.
ghs.assessment: いろいろ says they came to buy various things during camp. 'Several times' changes variety of purchases into frequency of visits.
ghs.remedy: Use 'We came here to buy all sorts of things during camp.'

highlights.text: Seems we came here several times to buy things during the Training Camp.

ghs.en: Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 合宿から帰ってくると、町から人はいなくなっていた。
rows.en: When we returned from camp, everyone in town was gone.

ghs.en: When we returned from the Camp, there was already no one in the town.

rows.jp: テレビ、ラジオ……あらゆるメディアが沈黙し、また電気や水道などの施設も止まっていた。
rows.en: Television, radio... every form of media had fallen silent, and utilities such as electricity and water had stopped as well.

ghs.en: TV, radio... all media silenced. Electricity, running water, all public services had stopped.

rows.jp: 皆、麻痺していた。
rows.en: We were all numb.

ghs.en: All of us simply paralyzed.
ghs.assessment: The source says everyone was numb or paralyzed. 'All of us simply paralyzed' omits the finite verb and narrows everyone to the narrator's group.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Everyone was numb.'

highlights.text: All of us simply paralyzed.

rows.jp: 棚上げするには重すぎる感情のやりとりが、直前にあったからだ。
rows.en: That was because emotions too heavy to set aside had passed between us immediately beforehand.

ghs.en: It shelved the exchange of depressing sentiments that was there just moments before.
ghs.assessment: The source explains that immediately beforehand they had exchanged emotions too weighty to set aside. The English says an unspecified 'it' shelved the exchange and reduces the weight to depressing sentiment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just before that, we'd had an emotional exchange too heavy to put aside.'

highlights.text: It shelved the exchange of depressing sentiments that was there just moments before.

rows.jp: 疲れて、話し合う気力もなく。
rows.en: We were exhausted, with no energy left to talk things through.

ghs.en: We were tired, without even the strength to discuss things.

rows.jp: 結論を保留したまま、別れた。
rows.en: So we parted with the matter unresolved.

ghs.en: We parted with all conclusions left pending.

rows.jp: そして今日。
rows.en: And now, today.

ghs.en: And then today.

rows.jp: 新学期。
rows.en: The new term.

ghs.en: A new school term.

rows.jp: 俺は普通に登校しようとしていた。
rows.en: I was trying to go to school as if everything were normal.

ghs.en: I was trying to attend as normal.

rows.jp: 扉を開く。
rows.en: I open the door.

ghs.en: I open the door.

rows.jp: 遮断されていた人の気配が溢れて、さらりと頬を撫でた。
rows.en: The presence of people, shut away until now, spills out and brushes lightly across my cheek.

ghs.en: The presence of a blockade of a person overflows and smoothly brush my cheeks.
ghs.assessment: The source says the pent-up presence of people spills out and lightly brushes his cheek. 'The presence of a blockade of a person' treats 遮断 as a blockade belonging to one person and fails subject-verb agreement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The pent-up presence of people spills out and lightly brushes my cheek.'

highlights.text: The presence of a blockade of a person overflows and smoothly brush my cheeks.

rows.jp: 窓際の席。
rows.en: The seat by the window.

ghs.en: In a seat in the row next to the window,

rows.jp: 立て肘をついて座っている少女が、ちらと一瞥をよこす。
rows.en: The girl sits with one elbow propped up and flicks me a glance.

ghs.en: there sat a girl, with her elbow on the table, sends a single peeking glance my way.
ghs.assessment: The source says a seated girl with her elbow propped gives him a fleeting glance. The English mixes 'there sat' with present 'sends' and adds a table not specified.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A girl sits with her elbow propped and flicks a glance my way.'

highlights.text: there sat a girl, with her elbow on the table, sends a single peeking glance my way.

rows.jp: 美しい長髪。
rows.en: Beautiful long hair.

ghs.en: Beautiful long hair.

rows.jp: それは神経質なほどの手入れによって保たれている、危うい整然。
rows.en: A precarious order maintained through almost neurotic care.

ghs.en: A systematicness that speaks of insecurity, maintained through a care at the limits of neurosis.
ghs.assessment: The source calls the order of her hair precarious, maintained by almost neurotically meticulous care. 'Systematicness that speaks of insecurity' changes precarious order into psychological insecurity and uses unnatural abstractions.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A precarious order maintained by almost neurotically meticulous care.'

highlights.text: A systematicness that speaks of insecurity, maintained through a care at the limits of neurosis.

rows.jp: 近くで見るとわかる。
rows.en: You can tell up close.

ghs.en: It's obvious when seen up close.

rows.jp: 鉄壁の管理は、ほつれ・枝毛の一本たりとも許していない。
rows.en: Her ironclad regimen permits not one stray hair or split end.

ghs.en: In the management of this impregnable fortress, not one fray, not one single split end can be allowed.

rows.jp: 触れると軽く、指で梳けばさらさらと砂のように流れる。
rows.en: Light to the touch; run your fingers through it, and it streams like fine sand.

ghs.en: Hers is a hair that with the lightest of touches sinks and slides through the fingers as if sand.
ghs.assessment: The source says the hair feels light and flows like sand when fingers comb through it. 'With the lightest of touches sinks' invents sinking and does not express the hair's lightness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It feels light, and when I comb it with my fingers it flows like sand.'

highlights.text: Hers is a hair that with the lightest of touches sinks and slides through the fingers as if sand.

rows.jp: はじめて会ったとき、彼女は無敵の鎧をまとっていた。
rows.en: When I first met her, she wore invincible armor.

ghs.en: The first time we met, she was clad in an impenetrable armor.

rows.jp: 近寄りがたい雰囲気という、見えない甲冑。
rows.en: Invisible armor: an air of unapproachability.

ghs.en: A mood of difficult approachability that turned into helmet and armor unseen.
ghs.assessment: The source apposes an invisible suit of armor: her unapproachable air. The English says a mood turned into armor, adds a helmet, and uses the unnatural phrase 'difficult approachability.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'An invisible suit of armor made of an unapproachable air.'

highlights.text: A mood of difficult approachability that turned into helmet and armor unseen.

rows.jp: 理由はいろいろあったのだろう。
rows.en: She must have had any number of reasons.

ghs.en: A variety of reasons, of course.
ghs.assessment: The source says there were probably various reasons. The fragment 'A variety of reasons, of course' omits the uncertainty and supplies unwarranted certainty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There were probably all sorts of reasons.'

highlights.text: A variety of reasons, of course.

rows.jp: ここが群青学院であること。
rows.en: The fact that this was Gunjo Academy.

ghs.en: What we have here, at Gunjou Institute,
ghs.assessment: This is one item in the list of reasons: that this place is Gunjou Academy. 'What we have here, at Gunjou Institute' changes the proposition and produces a broken continuation into the next line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The fact that this was Gunjou Academy.'

highlights.text: What we have here, at Gunjou Institute,

rows.jp: けたたましいクラスメイト。
rows.en: The clamorous classmates.

ghs.en: are clamorously wild classmates,

rows.jp: 死人のようなクラスメイト。
rows.en: The corpse-like classmates.

ghs.en: and corpse-like classmates.

rows.jp: ただ自らの世界しか見ていない虚ろな少年少女たち。
rows.en: The hollow boys and girls who saw nothing beyond their own worlds.

ghs.en:
Hollow boys and empty girls that cannot see but
their own world.

rows.jp: まともに会話が成立する者など、数えるほどしかいない。
rows.en: Only a handful of them could sustain anything resembling a normal conversation.

ghs.en:
The ones who can even establish the most basic
and upfront of conversations are but a handful.
ghs.assessment: まともに means properly or coherently. 'The most basic and upfront of conversations' adds a superlative and an unrelated claim of frankness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Only a handful of people could hold a coherent conversation.'

highlights.text:
The ones who can even establish the most basic
and upfront of conversations are but a handful.

rows.jp: 各所に立つ、感情を抱かない警備員たち。
rows.en: The emotionless guards stationed everywhere.

ghs.en:
Standing here and there, entertaining no emotions,
the guards.

rows.jp: 躁狂めいて戯画化された教室世界。
rows.en: A classroom world rendered as a manic caricature.

ghs.en:
The world of this classroom is a wild, ferociously
manic caricature.

rows.jp: 屍の山に、ゼンマイ仕掛けの玩具を放り込んだが如く、悪辣な世界観。
rows.en: A vicious world, as though someone had thrown windup toys onto a mountain of corpses.

ghs.en:
It's a horrifying view of the world, that
resembles a wind-up toy's as released into
a mountain of corpses.
ghs.assessment: The source calls the worldview vicious, like throwing a wind-up toy into a mountain of corpses. 'Horrifying' changes the judgment, and 'a wind-up toy's as released' is syntactically broken.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A vicious worldview, like a wind-up toy tossed onto a mountain of corpses.'

highlights.text:
It's a horrifying view of the world, that
resembles a wind-up toy's as released into
a mountain of corpses.

rows.jp: 適応係数４６、桐原冬子がその中で生きるには、残された５４％を守るものが必要だった。
rows.en: For Touko Kirihara, adaptation coefficient 46, to live within it, she needed something to protect the remaining 54 percent.

ghs.en: With a Conformity Coefficient of 46, for Kirihara Touko to live in that midst, defending the remaining 54% is a necessity.
ghs.assessment: The source says Touko needed something to protect the remaining fifty-four percent. 'Defending the remaining 54% is a necessity' removes Touko as the experiencer and is awkwardly nominal.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Touko needed something to protect the remaining fifty-four percent.'

highlights.text: With a Conformity Coefficient of 46, for Kirihara Touko to live in that midst, defending the remaining 54% is a necessity.

rows.jp: 他者を疎外することで、保たれる自意識。
rows.en: A sense of self preserved by shutting other people out.

ghs.en: A preservation of self-consciousness maintained through the alienation from others.
ghs.assessment: The source says her self-awareness is preserved by her alienating other people. 'Alienation from others' can instead mean that others alienate her, erasing her agency.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A sense of self preserved by shutting others out.'

highlights.text: A preservation of self-consciousness maintained through the alienation from others.

rows.jp: その意味で、入学当初における彼女の選択は正しかった。
rows.en: In that sense, the choice she made when she first enrolled was the right one.

ghs.en: In that sense, the selection she made shortly after enrollment was correct.

rows.jp: 今の冬子は、当時の彼女と似ている。
rows.en: The Touko of today resembles the girl she was then.

ghs.en: The Touko of now so resembles herself in those early days.

rows.jp: 虚飾と、虚勢と、虚栄心。
rows.en: Pretense, bravado, and vanity.

ghs.en: Affectation, bluffing, conceitedness.

rows.jp: それが桐原冬子という人物の全てと言えた。
rows.en: You could say that was all there was to Touko Kirihara.

ghs.en: Those were all the words that could be said about the personality that is Kirihara Touko.
ghs.assessment: The source says those traits could be called everything there was to Kirihara Touko as a person. The English changes that claim into one about all words that could be said about her personality.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That could be said to be everything Kirihara Touko was.'

highlights.text: Those were all the words that could be said about the personality that is Kirihara Touko.

rows.jp: 「へえ、来てたんだ」
rows.en: “Oh. You’re here.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ehhh, you came."
Touko: "..."

rows.jp: 視線が窓の外に投じられる。
rows.en: Her gaze shifts out the window.

ghs.en: Her eyesight is thrown to outside of the window,
ghs.assessment: The source says she directs her gaze outside the window. 'Her eyesight is thrown to outside of the window' substitutes the faculty of sight and is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She casts her gaze out the window,'

highlights.text: Her eyesight is thrown to outside of the window,

rows.jp: そらぞらしいほどのタイミングで。
rows.en: With timing so transparently contrived.

ghs.en: with a timing that is hypocritically false.
ghs.assessment: そらぞらしい describes timing so pointedly feigned or artificial that it is obvious. 'Hypocritically false' assigns moral hypocrisy and does not describe the staged timing.
